key_insight: Viscoelasticity makes electroconvection non-monotonic in Wi: instability is strongest near Wi ~ O(1) because stress–deformation phase relations weaken negative polymeric work and alter which eigenmode sets the threshold.
engineering_relevance: Tuning polymer elasticity can either suppress or amplify electroconvective mixing and should be accounted for when designing ion-selective devices, desalination systems, and electrochemical transport processes.
method: Linear stability analysis across Weissenberg number and wavenumber.
Eigenspectrum analysis to identify the mode selected at onset.
Mechanical-work decomposition into electric, solvent-viscous, and polymeric pathways, with polymeric work split into normal-stress-difference and shear-stress contributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a non-monotonic Wi dependence with a maximum growth rate and minimum critical voltage near Wi ~ O(1), plus an additional low-wavenumber minimum at intermediate Wi that disappears at large Wi.
watch_item: The mode-selection picture and asymptotic pathway ordering may be sensitive to model assumptions and parameter regime, so results should not be generalized beyond the analyzed viscoelastic electrolyte setting.
paper_title: Linear stability of electroconvection in a viscoelastic electrolyte: polymeric-work pathways and eigenmode selection
